ledger.x: 1918: Czechoslovakia is proclaimed; 'Czechoslovakia was founded in October 1918', Masaryk first president from 14 November 1918.
1919, January: fighting over Cieszyn Silesia (Teschen).
1919, April: Czechoslovak troops establish control in Carpathian Ruthenia.
1920, 28 July: the Spa Conference divides Cieszyn Silesia.
1920, 28 July: Czechoslovakia receives 58.1% of Cieszyn Silesia, by decision of the Spa Conference.
1938, October: Munich.
1938, 2 October: Poland annexes Trans-Olza after an ultimatum of 30 September: 'On 2 October, the Polish Army annexed an area of 801.5 km2 with a population of 227,399 people'.
1938, 2 November: the First Vienna Award gives Hungary southern Slovakia and southern Carpathian Ruthenia.
1939, 14 March: Slovakia secedes.
1939, 15-18 March: Hungary annexes Carpathian Ruthenia.
1939, March: Germany occupies the Czech lands and sets up the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia, proclaimed on 16 March 1939.
1945: 'Following Allied victory and the defeat of Nazi Germany in 1945, the Sudetenland was returned to Czechoslovakia.'
1945: Trans-Olza returns to Czechoslovakia.
1945: Slovakia and the south of Slovakia return to the restored state.
1945, May: the state is re-established.

1945, June: Czechoslovakia cedes Carpathian Ruthenia to the Soviet Union: 'Czechoslovakia signed a treaty with the Soviet Union, officially ceding the region' (the Red Army had secured most of it by 28 October 1944).
1960: the state 'officially became a socialist republic', the Czechoslovak Socialist Republic; colour and dossier continue.
1968-1969: the state is federalised into the Czech Socialist Republic and the Slovak Socialist Republic; the page gives '1968-1969', the year 1969 is the researcher's choice.
1990, 29 March: 'socialist' is dropped and 'federal' added; the state is the Czech and Slovak Federative Republic.
1992, 31 December: Czechoslovakia splits into the Czech Republic and Slovakia.

wars.name: Fighting over Cieszyn Silesia (Teschen)
wars.outcome: Interim division of 5 November 1918, invasion of 23 January 1919, battle at Skoczow 28-30 January, cease-fire 3 February 1919; the Spa Conference gives Czechoslovakia 58.1% of the area on 28 July 1920.

wars.name: Czechoslovak campaign against the Hungarian Soviet Republic in Carpathian Ruthenia
wars.outcome: Czechoslovak Army troops defeated local militias of the Hungarian Soviet Republic and by April 1919 'Czechoslovak control on the ground was established'.

wars.name: Dismemberment of Czechoslovakia (Munich Agreement to the occupation)
wars.outcome: Munich (30 September 1938), Polish annexation of Trans-Olza (2 October), First Vienna Award (2 November), Slovak secession (14 March 1939), Hungarian occupation of Carpathian Ruthenia (15-18 March) and the Protectorate (16 March).

wars.name: World War II
wars.outcome: The Czech lands are occupied as the Protectorate until the re-establishment of 10 May 1945; the government in exile sits in London; Carpathian Ruthenia passes to the USSR in June 1945.

certainty.note: Borders were still being fixed by interim agreements and fighting (Cieszyn Silesia, Carpathian Ruthenia, Slovakia).
Treaty lines (Saint-Germain, Spa 28 July 1920); the Hlucin and Valtice adjustments are not dated by the pages opened.
Munich, the Polish annexation, the Vienna Award line and the March 1939 partition changed the lines within months; the Munich page gives areas only for Trans-Olza and the Hungarian cession.
Treaty border with the USSR from June 1945; the 1920 lines restored; no change to 1992.
